subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The remaining blocker is choosing the permanent public config and security boundary; the code does not yet encode a clear cron policy layer to repair mechanically.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent first-class cron policy with documented precedence and delivery tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron runs as a subagent-like policy target, reducing config surface but coupling cron semantics to subagent behavior.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Leave global cron restrictions out of core and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, prompts, and delivery safeguards for individual jobs.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent first-class cron policy with documented precedence and delivery tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current signal for the overlapping cron/tool-policy product boundary and has already reviewed this issue path.
